summary: Service Worker interception duplicates SSE frames and 'last-event-id' offsets mismatch on reconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using our JS SDK behind a Service Worker are receiving duplicated SSE fragments and seeing a mismatch between the server-side "last-event-id" offset and the client resume token. This leads to partial duplicated sentences in the feed on reconnect and sometimes missing final punctuation.

Impact:
- A handful of dedicated customers (notably Streamly.ai) report corrupted transcripts and partial duplicates in live transcripts.
- Visible to end-users as repeated phrases, truncated final sentences, or missing terminal metadata on reconnect.
- Affects streaming features (chat and streaming transcription) and can cause automated downstream processors to mis-handle events.

Environment:
- prod - us-west-2 behind our edge-proxy and an in-customer Service Worker that intercepts fetch and forwards to EventSource/ReadableStream polyfill.
- Browsers reproduced: Chrome 115+, Chromium-based (observed); Safari unaffected so far.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Install Streamly.ai web app with Service Worker enabled which intercepts network and proxies to a local Response stream.
2. Start a streaming transcription session via SDK (SSE fallback path used).
3. Force a short network hiccup (disconnect for ~2s) or call client.reconnect().
4. Observe duplicated chunks and a resume that requests last-event-id=123 but server expects offset 122 (or vice versa) leading to replay or gap.

Observed behavior:
- SSE data frames appear twice in a short window after reconnect.
- Server logs show resume requests with last-event-id that does not match internal token sequence used by router (offset drift).
- SDK on the client reassembles messages but ends up with repeated phrases and occasionally an incomplete closing JSON metadata object.

Expected behavior:
- Service Worker should pass through streaming frames without duplicating; resume last-event-id should match server-side offset and deliver exactly-once message semantics (or clear idempotency markers).

Temporary workaround:
- Customer disabled Service Worker streaming interception and observed immediate return to normal behavior.
- Recommended short-term mitigation: advise customers to avoid Response body teeing in Service Worker or use a simple pass-through fetch.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-10]: Opened on behalf of Streamly.ai — customer reports repeated phrases and missing final punctuation after reconnects. Provided initial logs and HAR from customer.
Marco Chen (SRE) [2026-03-10]: Assigned. Requesting exact Service Worker script and Chrome version. Asked customer to reproduce with chrome://net-internals capture if possible.
Priya Nair (CS) [2026-03-11]: Customer confirms disabling the SW fixed symptoms. They can share the SW code under NDA. Asked for an explanation of why SW cause duplication.

Marco Chen (SRE) [2026-03-11]: Initial hypothesis: SW uses respondWith + readableStream tee which can cause the underlying fetch to be consumed twice in some Chrome streaming edge cases leading to duplicate data sent to SDK layer. Also seeing last-event-id header rewritten by SW in some builds causing offset drift.

Danielle Park (Frontend Eng) [2026-03-12]: Reproduced locally with a minimal SW that tees the response and forwards to two consumers — observed duplicate event delivery in Chrome and offset mismatch on reconnect. Filed a small repro sandbox.

Marco Chen (SRE) [2026-03-12]: Pushed edge proxy logging change to correlate incoming last-event-id with our router token on resume. Will coordinate with SDK team to add defensive dedupe for identical consecutive fragments.
Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-12]: Notified customer we're investigating and suggested temporary SW disable. Customer accepted and is testing a fix in staging.

Marco Chen (SRE) [2026-03-12]: Planned next steps: patch SDK to ignore duplicate consecutive SSE payloads for 250ms window, update docs with SW guidance, and add a Note in Console streaming docs about SW teeing pitfalls.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Collected server-side logs showing resume token sequences and last-event-id values. Found examples where client requested last-event-id=245 but router state advanced to 246, leading to a one-offset replay or drop.

2026-03-11: Customer SW uses response.clone/ReadableStream tee pattern and an EventSource polyfill. Chrome's implementation will sometimes re-emit identical underlying chunks to both tees which caused the SDK to see duplicates when SW forwarded both streams into the same client context.

2026-03-12: Reproduced with minimal SW: if the SW calls response.body.tee() and routes both readers through separate async pipelines that re-emit to the same client endpoint, we can observe duplicate events. The duplicate arrival timing can change last-event-id calculation if the client computes offsets per-reader rather than globally.
2026-03-12: Confirmed Safari doesn't show the issue likely due to different stream semantics. Issue appears Chrome-specific (Chromium streaming engine behavior + SW tees).
2026-03-12: Edge-proxy was sometimes rewriting newline boundaries when SW re-streamed payload; that contributed to partial JSON metadata corruption on boundary duplicates.
Hypothesis: Two cooperating factors — SW tee duplication + edge newline coalescing — combine to produce duplicate text fragments and occasional clipped JSON metadata on reconnect.
resolution:
Mitigation steps in progress:
1) Short-term: Advised customer to disable SW streaming interception (confirmed fix).
2) SDK: Implemented client-side defensive dedupe — ignore identical consecutive SSE payloads within a 250ms window and treat resume idempotently. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/915.
3) Edge: Added logging to correlate incoming last-event-id to router offset and detect drift early.
4) Docs: Add 'Service Worker guidance' note alerting developers to avoid response.tee patterns for streaming endpoints.
5) Long-term: Engineering to investigate protocol-level resume guards (server-side idempotency tokens) and potential header patterns to prevent offset drift when intermediaries rewrite requests.

Status: Patch staged for SDK dedupe and doc update; customer verified workaround. Scheduling a follow-up with Platform Eng to design server-side hardening.
